title: Cloud-Managed Model Compute Runbook
summary: Use managed cloud compute as a replaceable deployment adapter while preserving exact model identity, tenant authority, evaluation, cost, telemetry, and recovery evidence.
prerequisites: An authorized cloud account, region, quota, network, identity, and cost owner
An approved model, runtime option, workload, and data-classification decision
Service, evaluation, capacity, telemetry, rollback, and incident requirements
Node.js 22 or later for the offline CommonJS decision exercise

sections.title: Preserve a portable service contract
paragraphs: Managed compute can delegate accelerator provisioning, image staging, endpoint hosting, metrics, and some scaling or patching work, but the operator still owns the workload claim, model and license decision, identity and authorization, data and network boundary, representative evaluation, capacity and cost limits, release disposition, recovery, and provider exit. Write the stable request, response, error, streaming, identity, and overload contract before choosing an adapter.

Microsoft Foundry managed compute is described in the cited Microsoft documentation as public preview, with no SLA, and Microsoft does not recommend it for production workloads. This runbook therefore treats the Foundry adapter as a qualification or non-production path unless a separately approved provider commitment exists. Do not represent a successful qualification as an actual deployment or as production readiness.

Record the cloud account, subscription or tenant, project, region, quota, and private endpoint identifiers in restricted operations records. Public and reusable evidence should name configuration fields without exposing secrets. The account and project boundary for this fictional packet is: account ACCT-FICTIONAL-042, project PROJ-MODEL-QUAL, region region-example-1, tenant TENANT-FICTIONAL, workload support-answering, users internal-support, data classification synthetic-only, and network boundary private-test-network. No real account, endpoint, model deployment, or paid cloud operation was used.

Pin the model revision or deployment artifact, runtime or versioned deployment template, region, deployment type, capacity, endpoint contract, authentication mode, network policy, content or safety configuration, application adapter, evaluation version, and release time. A deployment name is only an operational handle, not sufficient build identity.

The fictional model example is Qwen, an open-weight model family associated with Alibaba. This packet intentionally does not assert a real Qwen revision, license, Foundry catalog entry, template, or API compatibility. The fictional evidence uses model identity Qwen-Fictional-7B, revision qwen-fictional-rev-2026-09-20, and template managed-template-fictional-v3. A real operator must verify the selected model, license, catalog support, template, and API compatibility for the target provider and date.

code.label: Portable contract and responsibility split
code.code:
Task: qualify a replaceable model-service adapter for synthetic internal-support requests.
Scope: account ACCT-FICTIONAL-042; project PROJ-MODEL-QUAL; region region-example-1; internal-support users; synthetic-only data; private-test-network; non-production qualification only.
Operator owns: workload claim; model and license decision; tenant, identity, and authorization; data and network boundary; request/response/error/streaming/overload contract; evaluation; capacity and cost limits; release disposition; telemetry interpretation; recovery; provider exit.
Provider adapter may handle: accelerator provisioning; runtime image staging; endpoint hosting; provider metrics; and some scaling or patching. Exact provider behavior must be verified for the selected adapter.
Exact fictional build: model Qwen-Fictional-7B; revision qwen-fictional-rev-2026-09-20; deployment artifact sha256:fictional-artifact-digest-042; runtime/template managed-template-fictional-v3; deployment type managed-instance; region region-example-1; two instances; two accelerators per instance; application adapter support-adapter-v2; content/safety configuration safety-config-v1; evaluation eval-support-v4; release candidate time 2026-09-20T18:00:00Z.
Endpoint contract: authenticated service identity only; POST /v1/generate; JSON request {input:string,maxOutputTokens:number}; JSON response {output:string,modelRevision:string,requestId:string}; errors are typed 4xx or 5xx JSON responses; streaming is disabled for this qualification; timeout is 30 seconds; overload returns 429; request and response bodies contain synthetic data only.
Permissions: model and license approval; subscription/project access; quota request; deployment; identity and role administration; network policy; release and rollback authority; cost-owner approval. Missing any permission blocks admission.
Provider boundary: Foundry managed compute is a provider-specific adapter, not the portable contract. A generic managed-compute provider may differ in model catalog, template, API, scaling, image, quota, billing, and network behavior. Requalify when changing adapter.

sections.title: Qualify quota, cost, telemetry, and failure behavior
paragraphs: Use the real gateway and authentication path to test routine, boundary, unauthorized, malformed, timeout, overload, dependency, and recovery cases. Measure latency and first-output distributions, throughput, rejection, model or accelerator saturation where available, warm-up, replica or instance behavior, quota, and attributable cost. Portal success and one playground response are smoke evidence only.

For this learning packet, every rate and measurement below is explicitly fictional. The rate is not an Azure quote, and the measurements are not actual GPU or endpoint benchmarks. Azure billing must be looked up for the current region, model/template, capacity, and date. The managed-compute billing unit described by Microsoft is accelerators per instance multiplied by instances multiplied by hours multiplied by rate. Specific rates, capacity, and quota are UNKNOWN until current provider lookup and an account-specific check establish them.

Fictional qualification limits are: maximum synthetic cost 45.00 currency units per test window; p95 latency at most 1000 milliseconds; rejection rate at most 0.05; evaluation score at least 0.95; maximum two instances; maximum four accelerators total; and recovery rehearsal must pass. These are decision thresholds for this exercise, not provider guarantees or service-level commitments.

Fictional positive measurements are: two accelerators per instance, two instances, eight hours, fictional rate 1.25 currency units per accelerator-instance-hour, calculated cost 40.00 currency units, p95 latency 820 milliseconds, rejection rate 0.02, evaluation score 0.96, warm-up 140 seconds, throughput 18 requests per minute, and recovery rehearsal passed. These values qualify only the stated non-production exercise when all evidence and permissions are present.

Test cases must include routine success; boundary token and concurrency values; unauthorized identity; malformed JSON and malformed fields; timeout; overload and 429 handling; dependency failure; quota exhaustion; telemetry loss; identity revocation; network denial; candidate rollback; reconciliation of in-flight work; and the documented alternative route. Record timestamps, request IDs, model revision, adapter version, status, latency, token or usage fields where available, and alert outcomes. Do not place keys, endpoint secrets, or sensitive request bodies in the reusable evidence packet.

code.label: decide.cjs, Node.js 22 or later offline capacity, cost, and release decision

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes authorization and role boundaries; model and license decision; exact deployment manifest; endpoint and network contract; negative access tests; representative evaluation; load and quota results; dated cost assumptions; correlated telemetry and alerts; rollback and alternative-route rehearsal; owners; residual risks; and review date. Keep environment identifiers, billing details, keys, and endpoint secrets in private operations records.

The filled fictional evidence packet has owner project42-editorial, operator release authority release-operator-042, cost owner finance-owner-042, evaluator eval-owner-042, and recovery owner incident-owner-042. The evidence date is 2026-09-20. The model/license record says Qwen-Fictional-7B, revision qwen-fictional-rev-2026-09-20, license decision FICTIONAL-APPROVAL-042, and explicitly states that no real license or catalog availability is asserted. The manifest records managed-template-fictional-v3, deployment artifact sha256:fictional-artifact-digest-042, managed-instance, region-example-1, two instances, two accelerators per instance, support-adapter-v2, safety-config-v1, and eval-support-v4.

Boolean evidence flags in this exercise are fictional trusted learning input. They are not authentication, approval, provider attestation, or independently verified evidence. A true flag means only that the exercise treats the corresponding evidence item as present. It cannot grant cloud access, permit a paid deployment, authorize production traffic, or substitute for an independently reviewed control.

Verification results in this packet are fictional: routine, boundary, unauthorized, malformed, timeout, overload, dependency, quota, telemetry-loss, identity-revocation, network-denial, rollback, and recovery cases were represented as PASS for the positive exercise. The synthetic evaluation score is 0.96 against a minimum of 0.95. Synthetic p95 latency is 820 milliseconds against a maximum of 1000. Synthetic rejection is 0.02 against a maximum of 0.05. Synthetic cost is 40.00 against a maximum of 45.00. These are not actual endpoint results. A real release requires reproducible test artifacts, timestamps, logs, dashboards, alert links, and provider-specific evidence.

Baseline decision: BLOCKED. The baseline input is missing modelLicense, negativeTests, costAssumptions, rollbackRehearsal, and alternativeAdapter evidence. It must remain blocked even if its numerical measurements look acceptable. Missing or invalid evidence never qualifies a release.

Positive decision: ELIGIBLE_FOR_QUALIFICATION_REVIEW. The positive input supplies every required evidence flag, recoveryPassed is true, calculated cost is 2 accelerators per instance x 2 instances x 8 hours x 1.25 = 40.00, and every measurement is within threshold. This is a review eligibility result only, not authorization for cloud operations, paid deployment, production use, or production readiness.
Changed budget decision: BLOCKED. Change only rate from 1.25 to 1.50. Cost becomes 48.00, exceeding the 45.00 budget, so the decision is blocked with BUDGET_LIMIT.

Stop admission when the deployment lands in an unauthorized boundary, artifact or policy identity drifts, protected data crosses its allowed boundary, a critical evaluation fails, quota or cost exceeds its decision, telemetry cannot support safe operation, or recovery is unavailable. Revoke or isolate the affected path, reconcile in-flight and external effects, restore the verified deployment or approved adapter, and repeat identity, access, quality, load, cost, and telemetry checks.

Recovery must explicitly address unknown in-flight work. First stop new traffic and record the last accepted request ID and provider status. Mark work whose completion is unknown as indeterminate, do not blindly replay non-idempotent requests, and reconcile with an idempotency key or an application-owned result ledger. Then revoke the failed route if needed, route only to the verified deployment or approved alternative adapter, verify response and error compatibility, and notify the workload owner. The alternative adapter is evidence only after its own model identity, policy, evaluation, cost, network, and rollback checks pass.

The fictional Qwen identity, revision, license decision, account identifiers, region, template, rate, capacity, quota, measurements, and test results are not real provider claims. Current provider rates, catalog support, capacity, and quota for region-example-1 and managed-template-fictional-v3 are UNKNOWN. A dated provider pricing or catalog lookup and an account-specific quota check would establish them.

code.label: Filled operating and evidence packet
code.code:
Task: Qualify a non-production, synthetic-only managed model-service adapter for internal-support requests.
Scope: Account ACCT-FICTIONAL-042; project PROJ-MODEL-QUAL; tenant TENANT-FICTIONAL; region region-example-1; users internal-support; private-test-network; no protected or production data; no production traffic.
Permissions: Model/license approval FICTIONAL-APPROVAL-042; project deploy permission; quota authority; identity and role administration; network-policy authority; release authority release-operator-042; cost owner finance-owner-042; recovery owner incident-owner-042. Any absent permission is a stop condition.
Exact build: Qwen-Fictional-7B; revision qwen-fictional-rev-2026-09-20; artifact sha256:fictional-artifact-digest-042; managed-template-fictional-v3; managed-instance; region-example-1; 2 instances; 2 accelerators per instance; support-adapter-v2; safety-config-v1; eval-support-v4; candidate time 2026-09-20T18:00:00Z.
Endpoint and network contract: private-test-network; authenticated service identity; POST /v1/generate; request {input:string,maxOutputTokens:number}; response {output:string,modelRevision:string,requestId:string}; typed JSON errors; 30-second timeout; 429 on overload; streaming disabled; synthetic data only.
Capacity and cost decision: accelerators per instance 2; instances 2; hours 8; explicitly fictional rate 1.25 currency units per accelerator-instance-hour; cost 40.00; maximum cost 45.00; maximum instances 2; maximum accelerators 4. The fictional rate is not an Azure quote. Current provider rates, capacity, and quota are UNKNOWN until looked up for the exact region, template, model, and date.
Verification: authorization; model/license record; manifest; endpoint/network contract; unauthorized and malformed tests; timeout, overload, dependency, quota, telemetry-loss, identity-revocation, and network-denial tests; representative eval; load and quota; cost assumptions; correlated telemetry and alerts; rollback rehearsal; alternative adapter evidence. Positive exercise records all required evidence as present and recoveryPassed true.
Provisional acceptance: synthetic p95 820 ms <= 1000 ms; synthetic rejection 0.02 <= 0.05; synthetic evaluation 0.96 >= 0.95; synthetic cost 40.00 <= 45.00. These are provisional learning values, not actual benchmarks or a production acceptance decision.
Stop conditions: unauthorized tenant, account, project, region, identity, or network; model, revision, license, template, artifact, policy, adapter, or evaluation drift; data violation; critical evaluation failure; quota or cost limit; missing telemetry or alerting; failed rollback or recovery; or unknown in-flight work that cannot be reconciled.
Recovery: stop new traffic; preserve request IDs and telemetry; revoke or isolate the affected route; reconcile in-flight and external effects using idempotency keys or the application result ledger; route only to the verified deployment or independently qualified alternative adapter; verify identity, access, quality, load, cost, telemetry, and error compatibility; record residual risk and review approval.
Release disposition: BLOCKED for the baseline missing evidence; ELIGIBLE_FOR_QUALIFICATION_REVIEW for the complete positive exercise; BLOCKED when the rate changes to 1.50 because calculated cost is 48.00 and exceeds the 45.00 threshold. No actual deployment claim is made.

sections.title: Changed-rate command
paragraphs: Run the same offline CommonJS decision script against the changed input.

sections.title: Changed-rate expected output and reasoning
paragraphs: The exact arithmetic is 2 accelerators per instance x 2 instances x 8 hours x 1.50 currency units per accelerator-instance-hour = 48.00. Since 48.00 is greater than maxCost 45.00, the result is BLOCKED with BUDGET_LIMIT. This is a qualification block, not evidence of provider failure.

sections.title: Portable file and command checklist
paragraphs: Create one file named decide.cjs containing the decision script. Create each JSON object in its separately labeled input section. Use Node.js 22 or later. The script reads a local file only and does not call a provider.

code.label: Copyable command sequence
code.code:
node --version
# Require Node.js v22 or later.
# Save the script as decide.cjs.
# Save the positive JSON as positive-input.json.
node decide.cjs positive-input.json
# Save the changed JSON as changed-input.json.
node decide.cjs changed-input.json
# Save the baseline JSON as baseline-missing-evidence.json.
node decide.cjs baseline-missing-evidence.json

sections.title: Source boundaries and provider verification
paragraphs: Microsoft documents the managed-compute billing unit as accelerators per instance multiplied by instances multiplied by hours multiplied by rate. Microsoft also documents managed compute as public preview with no SLA and not recommended for production workloads. Deployment templates are versioned, so model and template catalog support and API compatibility require verification for each model, template, provider, and date.

The terms used here are: acceleratorsPerInstance, the number of accelerators provisioned per compute instance in a managed-compute deployment; and managed compute, provider-managed accelerator provisioning, image staging, and endpoint hosting for model inference. The source materials do not establish a current rate, quota, capacity, catalog entry, or API compatibility for the fictional identifiers in this packet.

code.label: Provider verification checklist
code.code:
Before any real operation, establish with dated provider records:
- Current rate for the exact region, model or deployment artifact, template, capacity type, and test window.
- Account-specific quota and available capacity.
- Model catalog support and license terms.
- Versioned deployment-template compatibility and API compatibility.
- Identity, network, endpoint, logging, rollback, and provider support behavior.
Until those records exist, the rate, capacity, quota, catalog support, and compatibility for the fictional example are UNKNOWN.
